about: Monthly climate normals (1991-2020) of one representative city per generator region, used by house_sim/generator/climate.py for generation-2 houses (docs/design/TIER1_SWEEP.md sections 13.1 and 13.2). Every list has 12 values, January to December. The values were transcribed offline from the published normals tables named in each region's source and rounded (temperatures to 0.1 C); spot-check against the source before quoting a number. Fields marked 'estimate' in a region's notes are derived or assumed, with the reasoning given there.

fields.wet_days: mean number of days with precipitation at or above wet_day_threshold_mm (the source's own threshold)
fields.snow_days: mean number of days with measurable snowfall (reference for checks; the weather process makes snow from cold precipitation)
fields.sunshine_frac: mean bright-sunshine hours divided by the astronomically possible hours (0..1)
fields.temp_sd_c: estimate: standard deviation of the daily mean temperature about its normal (C)
fields.spell_h: assumption: mean duration of the rain spell on a wet day (h); short convective summer showers, long stratiform winter rain
fields.wet_day_offset_c: estimate (calibrated): how much warmer (+) or colder (-) a wet day runs than the month's normal, dry days taking the opposite share so the monthly normals hold; set in the cold months so that the process reproduces snow_days under the source's own definition (0 where the uncorrelated process already does)

constants.doc: TIER1_SWEEP 13.2: AR(1) daily temperature anomaly (phi 0.7, 21 terms), daily-low noise 0.5 C, two-state Markov wet days with persistence 0.3 (30-day burn-in), storm at 15 mm/h and above, a rate under 0.05 mm/h is a trace (no rain, the sky stays cloudy), snow at or below 1.0 C (the air temperature at which half of the precipitation over land falls as snow: 1.0 C over the Northern Hemisphere, Jennings et al. 2018 Nature Communications 9:1148; about 1.2 C, Dai 2008 GRL 35:L12802; the 13.2 sketch said 0.5 C) (10:1 snow ratio: 1 mm of water is 1 cm of snow), log-normal daily wind (sigma 0.35), +30 % afternoon wind, gusts 1.5 x the mean wind, daily maximum at 15:00.

us.source: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991-2020, Philadelphia International Airport (temperature, precipitation, days with >= 0.01 in, days with >= 0.1 in of snowfall); wind and percent of possible sunshine from the NOAA Local Climatological Data annual summary for Philadelphia
us.notes: temp_sd_c is an estimate (synoptic variability of a continental east-coast winter is large, about 5 C; humid summers vary about 2.5 C). spell_h is an assumption (frontal winter rain, convective summer showers). wet_day_offset_c is calibrated (480 simulated seasons) against snow_days with NOAA's definition (>= 0.1 in of snowfall, taken as >= 0.25 mm of water): Philadelphia's winter precipitation is mostly warm-sector and coastal-storm rain (the rain-snow line runs along I-95) while its coldest days are dry; capped at 4 C, the process still makes about 11 snow days against 9.8 (December 2.2 against 1.5).

uk.source: Met Office UK climate averages 1991-2020, Heathrow (max/min temperature, rainfall, days of rain >= 1 mm, sunshine hours); snow days and mean wind from the Met Office regional climate summary for southern England
uk.notes: sunshine_frac = sunshine hours / (day length x days) at 51.5 N. temp_sd_c is an estimate (maritime climate: about 3.5 C in winter, 2.5 C in summer). spell_h is an assumption. wet_day_offset_c is 0: London's wet winter days come with mild Atlantic air as often as with cold spells; the Met Office's days of sleet or snow falling (8.1) include showers and flurries on days below 1 mm, which the process does not make, so it shows about 6 days of measurable snow.

eu.city: Frankfurt am Main (airport), the documented German baseline for region eu
eu.source: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) Klimareferenzperiode 1991-2020, Frankfurt/Main station (temperature, precipitation, days >= 1 mm, sunshine duration, snowfall days, wind)
eu.notes: sunshine_frac = sunshine hours / (day length x days) at 50 N. temp_sd_c is an estimate (transitional climate between London and Toronto). spell_h is an assumption. wet_day_offset_c is 0: the uncorrelated process already makes about 19 snow days against DWD's 20.

jp.source: Japan Meteorological Agency normals 1991-2020, Tokyo (daily maximum and minimum temperature, precipitation, days >= 1.0 mm, days with snowfall, mean wind speed, sunshine duration)
jp.notes: sunshine_frac = sunshine hours / (day length x days) at 35.7 N. temp_sd_c is an estimate (sheltered maritime winter, humid summer: about 2 C). spell_h is an assumption (long tsuyu rain in June, short August showers, typhoon rain in September-October). wet_day_offset_c is calibrated (480 simulated seasons) against JMA's snow days (snow or sleet observed): Tokyo's winter precipitation comes with south-coast cyclones drawing cold air from the north-east while its dry winter days are sunny and mild; capped at -4 C, the process makes about 6.6 snow days against 7.2 (JMA also counts flurries on days below 1 mm, which the process does not make).

ca.source: Environment and Climate Change Canada, Canadian Climate Normals 1991-2020, Toronto Pearson International Airport (temperature, precipitation, days with >= 0.2 mm, days with >= 0.2 cm of snowfall, wind speed, bright sunshine)
ca.notes: sunshine_frac = sunshine hours / (day length x days) at 43.7 N. temp_sd_c is an estimate (continental winter with Arctic outbreaks: about 6 C). spell_h is an assumption. wet_day_offset_c is calibrated (480 simulated seasons) against ECCC's snow days (>= 0.2 cm of snowfall, taken as >= 0.2 mm of water): Arctic outbreaks are dry and clear, precipitation comes with milder air; the process makes about 44 snow days against 43.5.
